summary:
Length-prefixed decoding with one pointer: read digits up to the next `#` to get the length `k`, then the next
`k` characters are the string, regardless of what they contain. Jump past them and repeat. The first `#` after
a length is always the length's terminator, because digits come first. O(n).

question.md:
Each string was written as `<length>#<string>`, all concatenated. The strings may contain `#` and digits and may
be empty. Recover the list.

- **Bundle up to 10⁵ characters.**
- **Always a correct packing.**

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Empty strings in the list (`0#`), which take no characters after the `#`.
- Strings that contain `#` or digits; these must be copied, not interpreted.
- Lengths with several digits (`12#…`).
- An empty bundle means an empty list.

think.md:
**Why splitting on `#` fails.** `['a#1', '', '12#']` packs as `"3#a#10#3#12#"`. Splitting on `#` would cut inside `a#1` and
`12#`. The `#` is only trustworthy in one place: right after a length.

**The format as phases.** Each item is: digits (the length `k`), a `#`, then exactly `k` characters. Because the
length is read first, we always know where the current item ends, so we never have to look inside it.

**Why the first `#` after the digits is the separator.** At the start of an item we're reading the length, and
lengths contain only digits. The first non-digit we meet is therefore the separator; a `#` inside the item comes
after it and is never examined.

approaches.title: Read the length, then jump

idea.md:
Keep a pointer `i`. Read digits up to the next `#` to get the length `k`. The item is the `k` characters
after the `#`. Jump to just past them and repeat until the end.

build: Take the next `k` characters as one item.

lines.text: The output list and the read pointer. C allocates `n / 2 + 1` slots, since every item takes at least two characters (`0#`).

notes.c: Every item takes at least 2 characters (`0#`), so `n / 2 + 1` slots are enough.

lines.text: Each pass decodes exactly one item.
Read the length one digit at a time until the `#`. This `#` is guaranteed to be the separator, because the item's content hasn't started yet.
The next `size` characters are the item, whatever they contain. Then jump past them to the next item's length.
The items in order, empty ones included.

complexity.md: **Time O(n):** each character is read once, either as a digit, the `#`, or copied as content. **Space O(n)** for the output.

walk.title: Read a length up to the next '#', then take exactly that many characters, whatever they are.

takeaways.md:
- **Length-prefixed encoding** handles any content: never search inside the payload.
- Trust a delimiter only where the format guarantees it.
- **Pitfalls:** splitting on the delimiter; reading only one digit of the length.
